item.description:
**The window no longer crashes at its narrowest.** Dragged as narrow as it goes, the host window aborted on the first group picked in the sidebar — 0.1.7 and every release before it. The middle column held no width of its own, so what it showed moved its minimum, and picking a group asked a window already at its narrowest to widen in the middle of a layout pass, which AppKit ends by throwing. The column now holds one width whatever it shows, so no selection can move it. You reached it by dragging the window right in; the window as it opens was never there.
**Sheets fit the window they open over.** At the default window size, 0.1.7's host editor hung below the bottom edge with Save under it. The editors and the import are now no taller than the room under the toolbar, and where that is less than they want, the host editor's command box gives way first — but only by what the form can spare, read off the form as drawn, so the rows keep their room. Settings opens as tall as its tallest pane, where General's last section and Terminal's Keyboard sat wholly below the edge, and the palette picker fits the window it opens over wherever a palette is chosen.
**The host list survives a narrow pane.** Every row now drops the same thing at the same width — its tags first, then its group — where each row chose for itself, so one host kept a tag beside the next host losing the same tag. The name column is as wide as the longest name in the list rather than a fixed 240, which at the default size stood mostly empty while every row gave up its tags; cards are 210pt at their narrowest, so two fit across the pane as it opens, where one column of wide cards left their words in the left quarter; and a card keeps its line of group and tags whether or not anything is on it, so a row of cards stands one height.
**A group picked in the host pane is selected, not opened.** Arrowing onto one replaced the list under the highlight, so ↓ could never get past the first group. It is selected now, and two clicks or ⏎ open it. The pane and the sidebar also agree about what they are counting: the sidebar heads its tree Groups, as the pane does, and the whole list counts every group as it counts every host, where "12 hosts, 2 groups" was said of four.
**The tab strip shares its room by what each name needs.** Short names give their spare width to long ones, down to a floor, before the strip scrolls — shared evenly, "This Mac — ~" was cut to "This…c — ~" with 65pt of the strip standing empty. A name too long for its share is cut in the middle and at its dots, never beside one, where "root@127.0.0.1:2" read "root@….0.1:2" and "127.0.0.1:2" read "127….1:2"; a second tab's number stays whole after it; an edge with tabs past it fades, where the first tab was shown sheared with nothing to say the strip scrolled; the tab in front scrolls back into view whenever the strip's width changes; and a tab's tooltip is its whole name, where it was the shell's own title. A local shell's tab says This Mac, as the inspector and SFTP call it, and the title bar says what the tab says.
**The inspector describes a machine typed into ⌘K, and a local shell.** It said "Nothing selected" for both, so a machine reached through Quick Connect could not be saved from anywhere in the window. A typed machine now has its address written as a listed host's, port and all, What will run, Open now listing the tabs on that same machine, and Save as Host…; a local shell has Open now with the shells on this Mac and which of them is in front. A host's Open now marks each tab as the strip does, where a tab that never connected was listed as open as a live one, and says In front on the one already there.
**A host SFTP cannot open says what it means and what to do.** The refusal is drawn as the terminal's card for the same failure — the headline red with its mark, ssh's own line boxed and first, the way on leading — where it was plain text with the retry last, so one failure looked like two different things in two windows. Every failure now offers Edit Host… as a terminal tab does, and Try Again reads the host from the list afresh, where it went again with the copy the side was pointed at and a host renamed in Edit Host… kept its old name.
**An SFTP side with nothing in it asks for a host.** While the right side was still waiting to be pointed somewhere it said "0 items", which reads as an empty folder, and drew an empty striped table under a sortable header. It asks for a host now, alone on the table's ground, and the other side's button says Copy rather than "Copy to Choose a host". A side re-pointed while it is still connecting opens where it points now, and what the first connection brings back is closed on arrival.
**Controls that were live and did nothing are greyed out.** In the SFTP window: a side's path field and its "…" menu while it lists nothing, ↑ at "/", Edit ▸ Delete with nothing selected, and New Folder's Create and Rename's button for a name they would refuse — they took one, closed the question and did nothing. New Folder also says where the folder goes, since ⇧⌘N acts on whichever side last had the keyboard. With SFTP in front the menu bar names its own keys: File's New Folder… and View's Refresh, with Reconnect giving ⌘R up.
**One setting has one name, and an inherited value reads value first.** Settings called the terminal's palette Palette under a header saying Colours, which is where an inspector's "System from Settings" sent you; it is Colours everywhere now. Agent forwarding reads "Carried from Production", or "Not carried by default" where nothing says, in both editors and both inspectors — the host inspector had no row for it at all — where it read "From Production — carried". A palette is chosen by looking at it everywhere one is chosen, through the same swatch and picker, where three places offered a menu of names. And no field's example names a host, group, user, key or tag that is in your list, where "bastion" in Production's Jump host read as Production going through it.
**The import says one thing about your SSH config.** What the file holds was said three ways in three places, two of them at once, and a config naming no machine was reported as no file at all. The path typed in has its `~` expanded, where the field's own example found nothing; the file is spelled "SSH config" wherever the app names it; and each tab is headed by the name and the line the welcome gives that source. Export… greys out with nothing to export and says a save the disk refuses, where it wrote an empty file and dropped every refusal without a word.
**Every deletion question ends the same way.** Delete Group… left out "This cannot be undone.", which every other one says, and said all of a group's hosts move to the top of the list — they land in Ungrouped, at its foot, and the groups inside it each become a group of its own, which is what the sidebar and the editors call those places.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside: Settings' own layout, the session cards drawn as one shape on the window's own ground, the palette swatch, the editors' captions standing in one column, and a long tail of alignment. Two walks through the whole window after 0.1.7 found all of it. The suite went from 759 checks to 806.

**The host editor shows its command the way the inspector does**, one argument a line, with a long one wrapping under itself. It was the line you would paste into a shell, cut to two lines, so a host behind a jump host showed a run of quote marks with its middle missing. A long command scrolls in a box of its own, and the editor is a little taller to make room for it.
**New Host says why Add is greyed out.** It said nothing until something was typed, while New Group warned that a group needs a name before anything had been typed at all. Both now say what is missing from the start, quietly, and warn only once you have begun.
**The import's "Put new hosts in" looks like a field.** It sat against the right edge of its row, where "optional group" read like a group already chosen. It is a box beside its label now, like every other field.
**The SFTP window no longer counts what is not there.** While its right side was still asking which host to show, that side said "0 items", which reads as an empty folder, and This Mac's button said "Copy to Choose a host". The side with nothing in it counts nothing now, and the button says Copy.
**Quick Connect knows a host you have saved.** Typing the address of a host already in your list showed the typed row as "Not in your list", right under that host. It now says "As typed, without web's settings" — web being the saved host — since connecting as typed leaves that host's key, jump host and options behind.
**Hide Beside says what it does.** With a tab shown beside the one in front, the Terminal menu's ⌘D item still said Show Beside, though pressing it closed the split. It says Hide Beside then.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 756 checks to 759. With these, everything the walk through the whole window after 0.1.4 found is fixed.

**The menus offer only what works.** With the SFTP window or Settings in front, New Host…, New Group…, New Local Shell, Import… and Quick Connect… were enabled and did nothing, and so was Shellhand ▸ SFTP with nothing to open it from. Reconnect was live on a local shell, which has no host to reconnect to. They grey out now. macOS's own window tabs are gone from View and Window, where they offered a tab bar and a second pair of tab items on the strip's own keys. And two tabs on the same host each get a ⌘ number of their own in the Window menu — "refuser" and "refuser (2)" — where both landed on one.
**Deleting a group says what really happens.** It said all of a group's hosts moved to the top of the list, when only the ones filed in it directly do: the groups inside it move up with their own hosts still in them. It says so now, and says that what the group gives those hosts — the user, the key, the palette — goes with it.
**The palette picker fits in Settings.** It was taller than the Settings window, which left its Done button below the window's edge. It now fits the window it opens over.
**The SFTP window opens with the keyboard in This Mac's list**, as the host window opens in its host list, rather than in the path field, where ↓, Space and ⌫ edited the path.
**The host editor speaks like the rest of the app.** Its inherited values say "from Production", as the group editor and the inspector do, and the settings it called Through and Agent are Jump host and Agent forwarding, as they are everywhere else.
Nothing else here is visible from the outside. The suite went from 753 checks to 756.
